transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?

Since my husband passed, it feels like everything inside me just shut down, and I can’t make myself do the things I used to care about. I just don't have the spirit in me to do much of anything anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way since your husband passed? Has it been most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Oh, it's been much longer than just two weeks, doctor. This numb, shut-down feeling has been creeping in since the first year after my husband passed, and it's been going on almost every single day for a little over two years now.
During this time, have you also been feeling depressed or hopeless most days, or is it mainly a sense of grief and missing your husband?

It doesn't really feel like active sadness or hopelessness, and it's different from just missing my husband. It feels like someone turned a switch off inside me, leaving me completely numb. I just don't have any drive or ability to care about the things I used to love anymore.
Have you had any changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration since this started? I’m trying to tell whether this is more like depression or a grief-related reaction.

My energy is completely gone, like a switch was turned off, and I barely manage to eat simple meals. I don't really pay attention to my sleep, but I can't concentrate on anything anymore—most days I just stare at the TV without really watching it. It's just this heavy, overwhelming emptiness that makes it impossible to do anything.
When you think about your husband, do you mainly feel longing and sadness about the loss, or do you feel persistently depressed, worthless, or guilty most days?

I don't really feel guilty or worthless, and it's not even a sharp longing anymore. It just feels like a profound numbness, as if a switch was turned off inside me and left me completely shut down. I'm just entirely empty and can't make myself care about anything anymore.
Over the past two years, have you felt depressed or hopeless most days, or had feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt? Or is it mainly numbness and loss of interest without those feelings?

It is definitely the numbness and the complete loss of interest, not feelings of guilt or worthlessness. For about two years now, it has felt like a switch was turned off inside me, leaving me totally shut down. I just can't find the drive to care about or do any of the things I used to love.
Over the past two years, have you also felt depressed, hopeless, or worthless most days, or has it mainly been numbness and loss of interest without those feelings?

It's mainly just that numbness and losing interest in everything, not feelings of hopelessness or worthlessness. It feels like a switch was turned off inside me, making everything feel heavy and far away. This numb state has been going on like this for a little over two years now.

Do you still spend a lot of time longing for your husband or feeling intense waves of grief when reminded of him, or is it mainly a persistent numbness and loss of interest without that strong yearning?

No, I don't really have those sharp waves of grief or longing anymore. It is just a persistent, heavy numbness, like a switch was turned off inside me and left me completely empty. I just can't bring myself to care about anything at all.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. I don't want to do anything like that, I just feel completely empty, shut down, and exhausted. It's more like I'm just existing without any energy left inside me.
Before your husband passed, had you ever had a similar period of feeling depressed, numb, or losing interest in things for at least two weeks? Or did this start only after his death?

No, I've never felt anything like this in my life before my husband passed. Before he died, I was always very active and social, busy with my quilting circle and organizing events at the church. This numb, shut-down feeling only started creeping in during the year after he passed, and it is unlike anything I've ever experienced.

Did these symptoms start only after your husband’s death, or did they begin before the loss or in response to another major stressor? Also, do you feel persistent sadness or hopelessness most days, or mainly numbness and loss of interest?

No, these feelings didn't start until the year after my husband passed away, and there wasn't any other stressor. It’s not really active sadness or hopelessness either, but more of a profound numbness and a shut-down feeling where I’ve completely lost my drive and interest in everything.

Have your symptoms been present only in response to your husband’s death, or did they begin before the loss or after another major stressor? Also, do you still feel mainly numb and uninterested, or do you often feel sad or hopeless most days?

They only started after my husband passed, creeping in slowly during the year after he died. I still feel mainly that profound numbness and lack of interest, like a switch was turned off, rather than active sadness or hopelessness.

Do you still find yourself strongly longing for your husband or feeling intense grief when you think about him, or has the main problem become a persistent numbness and loss of interest that is no longer tied to reminders of him?

Yes, doctor, the main problem now is definitely that deep numbness and complete loss of interest, rather than active grieving or longing. It feels like a switch was turned off inside me, and it has been this way constantly for over two years now. I just have a total inability to care about or do anything at all.

Have you had changes in sleep or appetite, such as sleeping much more or less than usual or losing/gaining weight without trying? These symptoms can help tell depression apart from a grief-related reaction.
I haven't really paid much attention to my sleep or whether my weight has changed. I just feel completely shut down inside, and I barely manage to make simple meals for myself.
Have you had any clear changes in your sleep, appetite, or weight since this started, such as sleeping much more or less than usual or losing/gaining weight without trying?

To be honest, I haven't really paid attention to my sleep or my weight since my husband passed. I only manage to eat simple meals these days because I've completely lost the drive to cook or care about much of anything anymore.
Have you had any clear changes in your sleep or weight since this started, such as sleeping much more or less than usual, or losing/gaining weight without trying?
Like I said, I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or my weight. I've just been so numb and shut down that I haven't been paying enough attention to notice things like that.

Have you been having any nightmares, intrusive memories, or feeling constantly on edge or startled since your husband passed away? These can point more toward a stress-related reaction than depression.
No, I haven't been having any nightmares or bad memories, and I don't feel constantly on edge or startled. It is really more of that heavy, numb, shut-down feeling rather than being on edge.
Since your husband passed away, have you had any flashbacks, nightmares, or strong physical distress when reminded of the loss, or has it mainly been numbness and loss of interest?

No, I haven't had any flashbacks or nightmares like that, it has just been almost entirely numbness and a complete loss of interest. It feels like a switch was turned off inside me, making everything I used to love—like my quilting, choir, and cooking—feel heavy and so far away. I just can't bring myself to care about any of it anymore.

Since your husband passed away, have you had any nightmares, intrusive memories, or feeling constantly on edge or startled? These symptoms would suggest a stress-related reaction rather than depression.
No, I haven't had any nightmares, intrusive memories, or felt constantly on edge or startled. I just feel completely empty and shut down inside, like there is nothing left.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to function in your daily life, like taking care of yourself, managing household tasks, or getting out of bed most days?

Yes, doctor, it has made daily life incredibly hard for me. I went from running church events and keeping my home spotless to barely managing to bathe, eat simple meals, or even open my mail. I’ve stopped seeing friends and going to church altogether because just leaving the house feels too overwhelming now.

Have you been feeling sad or hopeless most days, or is it mainly a loss of interest and numbness without feeling depressed? Also, did these symptoms start only after your husband’s death or did they begin before that?

It is definitely a complete numbness and loss of interest rather than active sadness, like a switch was turned off inside me and I just can't bring myself to care about anything anymore. These feelings only started creeping in during the year after my husband passed away, and I never felt anything like this before his death.

Did your symptoms start within a few months of your husband’s death, or did they begin later and persist for a long time afterward? Also, do you find yourself missing him intensely, or is it mainly a numb loss of interest in everything?

They didn't start right away, but crept in over the first year after he died and have persisted for over two years now. It isn't intense yearning or active crying, but a profound, numb loss of interest in everything, like a switch was turned off inside me. I just can't bring myself to care about or do the things I used to love, like choir and quilting.
Did your symptoms begin within 1 month after your husband’s death, or did they start later than that?
No, they didn't start right away within that first month. It was a gradual thing that started creeping in during the first year after he passed away.
Did your symptoms start within 1 month after your husband’s death, or did they begin later than that?
It didn't start within that first month, no. It was much slower than that, just creeping in little by little over the first year after he passed away.
Did these symptoms begin within 1 month after your husband’s death, or did they start later than that?

No, it didn't start right away in that first month; back then, I was just grieving like anyone would. This deep numbness and shut-down only started creeping in later on, during the first year after he passed, and it has stayed with me for over two years now.
Did your numbness and loss of interest start within 1 month after your husband’s death, or did it begin later than that?

Like I mentioned, it didn't start within that first month. It crept in gradually over the first year after he passed, starting with what everyone thought was normal grief and slowly turning into this complete lack of interest and energy.
Did the numbness and loss of interest start within 1 month after your husband’s death, or did it begin later than that?

No, it didn't start within that first month at all. It crept in gradually over the first year after he passed, starting as normal grief before slowly turning into this deep, persistent shut-down feeling. It's just been like that ever since.
Did the numbness and loss of interest begin within 1 month of your husband’s death, or did it start later than that?
No, it didn't start within that first month at all. It crept in gradually over the first year after he passed away, slowly getting worse over time until I just shut down completely.
Did the numbness and loss of interest begin within 1 month of your husband’s death, or did it start later than that?
No, doctor, it didn't start right away in that first month. It was a very gradual change that started creeping in during the first year after he passed away, rather than happening immediately.
Did your symptoms start within 6 months of your husband's death, or did they begin later than that? This helps me tell whether this is more likely a grief/stress reaction or a depressive episode.
No, they didn't start within those first six months. It was a very gradual change that only started creeping in later on, during that first year after he passed away.
